Subject: Potential distribution + governance for OpenForge weights

Hi Irene / Camila,

Thanks for taking a look at this. OpenForge is preparing a limited-distribution release of a new 16B open transformer (OF-16B) and we'd like Redwood to be a preferred distribution partner for hosted access and allowed redistribution to ISV partners under a controlled CLA.

High level ask: can Redwood host OF-16B behind your dedicated and hosted offerings while honoring a publisher governance model that includes:
- attribution and branding in the model card
- embargoed redistribution to certified ISVs only (we provide the cert list)
- instrumentation for provenance metadata in inference requests (model id + publisher signature)

Attached is our initial MLA (OpenForge_MLA_v1.pdf) — this is an early draft to seed conversation. Key commercial asks are modest revenue share for redistributed weights and a "publisher opt-out" clause for future derivatives.

Are you available for a quick 30-min sync this week? OpenForge legal can join if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of Partnerships
OpenForge Labs

Irene / Sergio — reviewed the MLA and put together a redline + summary. Main points:
1) Redistribution scope: accept certified-ISV-only redistribution but require DocuSign-based CLA execution + automated flagging in our onboarding system. This mitigates liability.
2) Opt-out on derivatives: we can accept a narrow opt-out (publisher can restrict commercial re-release of derivatives built from their weights) provided: (a) the restriction is timeboxed (e.g., 12 months), (b) we keep a rollback path for customers if the publisher revokes later, and (c) we have a defined dispute process.
3) Revenue share: propose a simple % of redistribution revenue with a reporting cadence (quarterly) and basic audit rights.
4) Provenance headers: ok as metadata; legal wants them redacted from any logs exported externally.

I attached a redline PDF (Redwood_OpenForge_Redline_v2.pdf) and a short checklist for operations. I recommend we:
- run a 30-min legal sync with OpenForge (include their legal counsel),
- scope the onboarding automation (DocuSign webhook + HubSpot enrollment flow), and
- define a minimal SLA for redistributed artifacts.

Marissa Cole
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the MLA. We had a legal pass and a short ops assessment. High-level agreement and next steps below: 

Agreed (high level):
- Redwood will be a preferred distributor for OF-16B for hosted and dedicated placements.
- Redistribution permitted only to DocuSign-executed certified ISVs (OpenForge will provide initial list).
- Publisher opt-out on derivatives acceptable if timeboxed (initial recommendation: 12 months) and tied to an explicit dispute resolution path.
- Revenue share to be agreed in the commercial sheet; Redwood recommends quarterly reporting and basic audit rights.
- Provenance headers will be emitted in telemetry and redacted from external logs; we'll add x-redwood-publisher-id as a standard header.

Immediate next steps:
1) Marissa to share the redline (done). Please have your counsel review and come back with any changes by 12/9.
2) Camila to draft the partner onboarding checklist and DocuSign flow; target pilot in Q1.
3) Schedule a 30-min cross-functional kick on Wed 12/9 10:00 PT to align (legal + ops + partnerships).

If this aligns, we'll circulate a short MOU and the signed redline to formalize. Excited to move forward.
